title: Modeling Annotator Disagreement with Demographic-Aware Experts and Synthetic Perspectives

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating the Mean Absolute Error (MAE) and correlation (Pearson's r) of model-predicted ratings against actual subjective annotations from different racial and ethnic groups across tasks like toxicity, offensiveness, and politeness.
Comparing model prediction accuracy and alignment for subjective NLP tasks across annotators of different gender identities.
Measuring performance disparities in predicting subjective NLP labels (e.g., patient-centered communication, offensiveness) across different annotator age groups.
Assessing how accurately the model captures the subjective viewpoints of annotators with different levels of educational attainment.
Evaluating the alignment of model predictions with the subjective ratings provided by annotators of various occupational statuses.
Measuring model prediction errors and alignment for toxicity labels assigned by annotators with varying political affiliations.
Evaluating model performance disparities in predicting toxicity annotations across different LGBTQ+ statuses.
